title: Make Pages edit mode usable on narrow viewports
description:
Problem: the deeper `/pages` edit-mode review showed the navigation tree still taking the upper portion of the viewport while the editor and live preview were reduced to short stacked panes. The markdown editor had only a small visible area, the preview was barely usable, and the edit toolbar included compact icon controls plus a file input affordance that need clearer hierarchy and accessible labeling.

Desired outcome: editing a page should provide a clear primary editor area, optional preview, and reachable formatting/media tools without fighting the navigation tree.

Scope:
- In scope: edit-mode responsive layout, editor/preview split or tabs, navigation auto-collapse/focus behavior, toolbar grouping, file/media control labeling, and save/cancel action hierarchy.
- Out of scope: changing markdown storage, page metadata schema, or renderer semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- At narrow widths, the markdown editor gets enough space for practical editing.
- Preview is available as a toggle/tab/focused pane rather than a tiny competing panel.
- Navigation remains recoverable but does not dominate edit mode by default.
- Toolbar/media controls have clear labels/tooltips and do not cause horizontal overflow.

Validation:
- Capture `/pages` edit mode at narrow and desktop widths with live preview on/off.
- Run focused browser checks for edit, toolbar actions, preview refresh, save, and cancel.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 deeper live review: Pages edit mode left the editor and preview as very short stacked panes while the navigation tree stayed open above them.
